<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/automation/flow-text-slot-template.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 713f231854cfbb115179096b2af1971afff14dbc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin aed8c24ce3397dd3039f9cfe7efb3d73804705fd && git checkout aed8c24ce3397dd3039f9cfe7efb3d73804705fd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 713f231854cfbb115179096b2af1971afff14dbc c7a71df7ecce8d8b9c6ff83bca00bfacd7cf2f4a && git checkout -B drift-repro 713f231854cfbb115179096b2af1971afff14dbc && git merge --no-ff c7a71df7ecce8d8b9c6ff83bca00bfacd7cf2f4a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 713f231854cfbb115179096b2af1971afff14dbc
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 713f231854cfbb115179096b2af1971afff14dbc` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c7a71df7ecce8d8b9c6ff83bca00bfacd7cf2f4a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23320 (body, triage `6152852815`, unlock `6156025101`, claim `6158190909`, os-dev-report `6160033902`); PR #23383 (body, 3-file list, net diff against `main`: +70/-4, comments only); the 43 check-runs on the head; the committed source at the head via `git show` / `git grep` on `origin/claude/issue-23320-slot-judges-at-parse` (tip = the head).

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set: unchanged — right.** The diff edits three docblocks and no schema, refinement, export or test. `FlowSchema`'s contract arm still exempts a slot token at `slotJudgeRefusedPaths` and adds no slot-judge issue; `parseEndNodeConfig` still applies `EndConfigSchema` to a top-level `end`. Nothing `FlowSchema.parse`, `defineStack`, `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, the `flow` metadata type or the environment artifact accepted or refused at base moves at this head.

**Public surface: one comment sentence published — right, and declared.** `packages/spec/package.json` `files[]` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts` at this head, so `flow.zod.ts`'s new sentence reaches the tarball; the two judge modules are `.ts`, not `.zod.ts`, so their module docs are repo-internal. The PR body states exactly this. The dev's local `check:api-surface` read "unchanged", and the CI spec gates on the head are green (Lint and Repo Gates, Spec property liveness: success).

**Factual claims in the new comments, each read at the head:**

- `registerFlow` parses first and a parse refusal reaches its caller as the parse's own issue list — TRUE. `engine.ts` `registerFlow` calls `canonicalizeFlow` (which runs `FlowSchema.parse`, throwing the ZodError) and only then iterates `registrationChecks`, throwing `new Error(refusal.message)` on the first refusal; the slot judges run inside `validateFlowExpressions`, one of those checks (`flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals` and `flowNodeTextSlotSources` plus `textSlotTemplateRefusal`, walked per graph with the node's id, type, slot label, config path and source).
- The `validateStackExpressions` rule, `expression-invalid` at `error`, run by `objectstack validate`, `objectstack compile` and the publish gate of an `active` save — TRUE. `authoring-rules.ts` registers it at tier `gating`, input `parsed`, surfaces `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, runtime types including `flow`, findings mapped to `EXPRESSION_INVALID = 'expression-invalid'`; `validate-expressions.ts` pushes both slot refusals at `severity: 'error'`; `validate.ts` and `compile.ts` each `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse` before `runAuthoringRules`; `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` returns an empty verdict unless `state === 'active'`. The cited pin `runtime-authoring-gate.flow-filter-operand.test.ts` exists and asserts `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 on an `active` save with `VALUE_SLOT_TEMPLATE_REFUSAL`.
- Every run, through the contracts composing `FlowValueSlotSchema` and the `assignment` executor's own call — TRUE. The CRUD, screen, subflow, map, notify and http executors call `parseNodeConfig` against their contract; `logic-nodes.ts` calls `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals('assignment', config)` itself (no executor contract parses an assignment config, as `flow.zod.ts` already says).
- The doors that reach `FlowSchema` — TRUE. `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` spreads `STACK_DEFINITION_COLLECTIONS_SHAPE`, whose `flows` is `z.array(FlowSchema)`; `defineStack` builds through it; `metadata-type-schemas.ts` maps `flow` to `FlowSchema`; `environment-artifact.zod.ts` wraps `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`.
- The contract arm stands aside at `slotJudgeRefusedPaths` — TRUE. `flow-node-config-refusals.ts` computes the set from both judges and `builtinValueJudged`'s last exemption skips those paths.
- The stored pass: a parse refusal reports the row `failed` and flips `storedMigrationClean`; a refusal after the parse is listed as a TODO and the verdict does not move — TRUE. `canonicalizeStoredFlow` runs the same `canonicalizeFlow` (so the parse throws out of it), `protocol.ts` catches into `outcome: 'failed'`, `storedMigrationClean` is `pending === 0 and failed === 0`, and `stored-migration.ts` states TODOs never move it; `migrate/meta.ts` reads that verdict for its exit code. The TODO listing is as written: registration refusals under `FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID = 'registerFlow'`, skipping a site a chain TODO already names, and `refused-shapes.ts` carries `flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused` at `toMajor: 18`.
- What the gap leaves (`os dev` / `os serve` boot, `registerFlow` refuses with its located line and does not register) — TRUE. Neither `dev.ts` nor `serve.ts` runs the authoring rules; `plugin.ts` wraps the boot-pull `registerFlow` in a try whose catch logs `[Automation] failed to register flow` and continues.
- Text-slot contracts `NotifyConfigSchema`, `HttpConfigSchema`, `ScreenConfigSchema`, `EndConfigSchema` — TRUE and complete. The four sites are `io-node-config.zod.ts` (notify templates and `actionUrl`; http `url` and each header) and `builtin-node-config.zod.ts` (screen `title` / `description`; end `message`); no other composer exists under `packages/spec/src/automation`. Adding `HttpConfigSchema` and the compile / publish-gate doors corrects the old list.
- "The flow parse runs this judge on one slot: a top-level `end` node's `message`" — TRUE as scoped. `parseEndNodeConfig`'s own docblock measures that a nested `end` is not refused at the flow parse, and `end` is structural with no executor, so `EndConfigSchema` has no door but the parse.

**One wording imprecision, not a false sentence:** `flow.zod.ts` says the parse "runs neither slot judge itself" and the text-slot doc says the parse "calls no slot judge of its own". Mechanically the parse does invoke both judges, inside `slotJudgeRefusedPaths`, to compute the exemption set; what is true, and what both sentences mean in context, is that no refusal of either judge is the parse's own (the `end` `message` excepted, through its contract). Both docs name `slotJudgeRefusedPaths` in the same breath, so a reader is not misled; a tighter verb ("emits neither slot judge's refusal itself") would close it. Non-blocking; a follow-up wording edit is enough.

### ② Semver level

**`skip-changeset` is right for this diff.** Nothing published changes in behaviour, accept set or export: the dev measured `dist/` free of the new text with a control phrase present, and the CI spec gates on the head are green. The tarball differs by one comment sentence in a shipped `.zod.ts` source. AGENTS.md reserves `skip-changeset` for "a diff that publishes nothing from any released package" and demands a `patch` for a bug fix; this PR fixes no code — the card closes by outcome (b), a measurement and its documentation — so the bug-fix clause is not triggered. Note for the seat: the dev's phrase "comment-only changes are on the no-publish fast track" has no AGENTS.md sentence I could find; the judgment above rests on the rule's own wording, not on a named fast track. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

**`Clause-②: no` (the PR body) is right; `no (narrowing)` (the claim) is not, for this diff.** Per AGENTS.md the `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING and summons `check:adr-0087-registration`'s disposition. The claim's arm was written for route (a); the landed diff narrows nothing, and `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` reads "adds no declared-breaking changeset". The seat amends its claim line rather than the dev restoring `(narrowing)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Outcome inside the triage direction: yes.** The triage's direction reads "If the seat finds the parse must not run the slot judges … it says why in that doc and closes the card with the measurement." The module docs say why, with the two measured reasons and the condition for revisiting; the PR body carries the measurement (route (a) applied at `ca829754b`, reverted at `d5b704543`, both present in the branch history; re-measured after `main` `dc393266f`). The file surface stays inside the claim's list (three of its named files; no test, no changeset — each declared).

Dev deviations, each answered:

1. **Clause-② line differs from the claim** — answered in ②: the PR body is right; the seat amends the claim.
2. **No `.changeset/23320-*.md`** — answered in ②: right for a comment-only diff.
3. **The triage's `defineStack` pins are not added** — ESCALATED to the seat. The triage's last direction sentence and the card's second "Wanted" bullet state the pins unconditionally; the dev declined them as "they would pin the gap itself". My reading: under outcome (b) the gap is now a documented, deliberate door split, and a pin of a deliberate contract is exactly what a pin is for — one value-slot token and one text-slot token accepted at `defineStack` and refused at `registerFlow`, with a CEL envelope and a `{{ }}` hole as the controls accepted at both. That would hold the module doc's claim mechanically at the door the card names. Against that: the split is already held indirectly, since route (a) turned the located-refusal pins red in `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/lint` and the stored-listing pins in `canonicalize-stored-flow.test.ts`, so the doors cannot silently move. Not a contract defect; the seat decides whether to accept the deviation or ask for the two pins on this branch before the queue.
4. **Measurement and revert commits kept in history** — fine: the net diff against `main` is the three comment edits; the squash merge carries none of the measurement.
5. **`origin/main` merged mid-run without `pnpm install`** — fine for this diff: nothing in three comment edits depends on the lock delta, and the merge brought #23356, which the text-slot doc's `registerFlow` TODO listing cites. The branch sits behind `origin/main` at my read (`28e294f45`); the queue re-bases.
6. **`@objectstack/cli` unit and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally** — the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts: Build Core success; Lint and Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · docs and code guards, the three scoped Lint jobs, Type Check · source gates, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the three claim/closing guards, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate, filter: success. Still in progress at my read: Test Core 1/6 through 6/6, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. Skipped (opt-in or matrix placeholders): Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, the Dogfood matrix placeholder, and one duplicate each of Check PR Size, Auto Label and Check Changeset. No check-run failed.
7. **The text-slot door list also gained `HttpConfigSchema` and the compile / publish-gate doors** — verified true at the head (①) and inside the claim's "module docs' door lists" surface.

`open_questions` (A: leave as documented; B: file the two engine-side preconditions, then a spec card): **A, answered, with one addition.** Every authoring door already refuses the token with its remedy; B costs an `engine.ts` change in a file other claims hold plus about fifty re-pins, for a residue no measured author hits. The module doc records the condition under which the judges can join the parse, which is where the next reader of this question will look. The addition: the dev's first out-of-scope finding ("noted, not filed") reads as a reachable prose defect — `os migrate meta --stored` prints "keep reading canonically through the chain, so nothing is broken" for a flow row `FlowSchema.parse` refuses, which the boot then refuses — owner the stored-preview lane (`domain:spec` seat 2). ESCALATED: the seat decides whether it is filed as a card. The second finding (the `lint-flow-patterns.test.ts` copy of the docs example drifting from the page's CEL envelope) is low and may be filed or left at the seat's call.
